sentences.text: The genus name refers to the complex tympanic pneumatic system of many cavities in the basicranium, a bone at the base of the skull.
The large supratemporal fenestrae are characteristic of longirostrine crocodilians, animals with elongated snouts.
The genus Eopneumatosuchus was named by Crompton and Smith in 1980, with the type species designated as Eopneumatosuchus colberti.
Fossils have been found in the Kayenta Formation of Arizona, located about 20 miles southeast of the Grand Canyon.
Fossil records for this animal include occurrences from two localities that are situated near each other.
Similar pneumatic cavities are found in protosuchians like Protosuchus and Hemiprotosuchus, but they are less elongated than in Eopneumatosuchus.
Eopneumatosuchus was initially classified as a protosuchian when it was named in 1980, but it is currently classified as a basal crocodyliform.
The animal is considered more derived than protosuchians like Protosuchus, which were found in the earlier Moenave Formation.
Eopneumatosuchus belongs to the parent group Crocodylomorpha and is classified as a reptile.
Fossils of Eopneumatosuchus date to the Early Jurassic, likely the Sinemurian stage, living between 199.5 and 184.2 million years ago.
